                  run_batch_corrected_data.txt

                  correlation_p_values.pdf  (uncomment pdf/dev.off to save)

  Authors       : Sadanandam Lab, Institute of Cancer Research, London
  Note          : Update the file path in Chunk 1 to point to your local copy
                  of the metabolomics data before running.

-->

## Step 1 – Load and filter metabolomics data

```{r load-data}
# Load the batch-corrected metabolomics matrix.
# Rows = metabolites, columns = patient samples (first column = metabolite name).
metab <- read.delim(
  "20200902_ColossusResults_Metabolomics_2_tissue_weight_Centre_run_batch_corrected_data.txt",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
dim(metab)  # confirm matrix dimensions

# Remove metabolites labelled "Unknown" — these lack HMDB IDs and are excluded
# from all publication figures.
unk         <- grep("Unknown", metab[, 1])
metab_known <- metab[-unk, ]
dim(metab_known)

# Filter to metabolites with SD > 1 across samples.
# This retains biologically variable features and reduces noise.
sd_metab   <- apply(metab_known[, -1], 1, sd)
w_sd_metab <- which(sd_metab > 1)
length(w_sd_metab)  # number of retained metabolites

metab_known_sd <- metab_known[w_sd_metab, ]
dim(metab_known_sd)

# Transpose to samples-in-rows format required for cor().
metab_known_sd_t <- t(metab_known_sd[, -1])
colnames(metab_known_sd_t) <- metab_known_sd$Metabolites

# Optional: save filtered matrix for downstream analyses (e.g. Fig 2D).
# write.table(metab_known_sd,
#   "results/2B_filtered_metabolites_sd1.txt", row.names = FALSE, sep = "\t")
```

## Step 2 – Compute Pearson correlations and generate annotated heatmap

```{r correlation-heatmap, fig.width=20, fig.height=15}
library(corrplot)
library(pheatmap)

# Compute pairwise Pearson correlation matrix across all retained metabolites.
corr_mat <- cor(data.matrix(metab_known_sd_t), method = "p")

# Diverging colour palette: red = strong positive, white = zero, navy = negative.
macolor <- colorRampPalette(c("red", "white", "navyblue"))(100)

# First pheatmap call is used only to extract the hierarchical clustering tree.
# The tree is cut in the next step to assign cluster membership labels.
plot_data_pheatmap <- pheatmap(
  corr_mat,
  color             = rev(macolor),
  clustering_method = "complete",  # complete linkage for compact, defined clusters
  fontsize_row      = 0.8,
  fontsize_col      = 0.8
)

# Cut the dendrogram into k = 4 clusters.
# Four clusters correspond to distinct metabolic pathway groups identified in
# the COLOSSUS data (amino acids, lipids, TCA intermediates, nucleotides).
tree_cut <- cutree(plot_data_pheatmap$tree_row, k = 4, h = 20)

# Build annotation data frame for heatmap sidebar labels.
tc <- data.frame(
  tip              = names(tree_cut),
  clust_membership = as.character(unname(tree_cut))
)
row.names(tc) <- tc$tip
tc <- tc["clust_membership"]

head(tc)   # inspect first few cluster assignments
str(tc)    # confirm data frame structure

# Final annotated heatmap — Figure 2B.
# Cluster bars appear on both rows and columns for a symmetric display.
# Uncomment pdf()/dev.off() to save the figure to file.

# pdf("results/2B_20260321_COLOSUSS_known_metabolites_sd1.5_metabolite_correlation_p_values.pdf",
#     width = 20, height = 15, paper = "a4r")
pheatmap(
  corr_mat,
  color             = rev(macolor),
  clustering_method = "complete",
  annotation_row    = tc,   # cluster membership shown as row sidebar
  annotation_col    = tc,   # same annotation mirrored on columns
  fontsize_row      = 0.8,
  fontsize_col      = 0.8
)
# dev.off()
```
